name: Reine Village
description: The village itself: a cluster of red rorbu cabins on stilts over the harbor, ringed by granite peaks with Reinebringen towering above. Walkable in minutes, it holds the main lodges, a grocery, and the classic view that makes Reine one of Norway's most photographed places.
pros: Rorbu cabins make superb home offices
cons: Almost no nightlife or nomad scene

name: Hamnoy
description: A short hop from Reine along the E10, Hamnoy is the tiny fishing hamlet behind Lofoten's most reproduced photo: red cabins clustered beneath sheer peaks, framed by the arcing bridge. It is minuscule and photogenic, with a handful of rorbu lodges and stunning outlooks in every direction.
pros: Arguably the most iconic view in Lofoten
Peaceful rorbu lodging on the water
Easy E10 access to Reine and beyond
cons: Popular photo spots can get busy in summer

name: Sakrisoy
tagline: The yellow cabins between the giants
description: A small islet between Reine and Hamnoy, Sakrisoy stands out for its ochre-yellow rorbu cabins, a contrast to the region's usual red. It offers cozy lodging, a well-known fish shop and eatery, and sweeping views of the surrounding peaks and water, all a few minutes from Reine.
pros: Distinctive yellow cabins and great views
Known local fish shop and dining
cons: Premium pricing like the rest of the area

name: A i Lofoten
tagline: The village at the road's end
description: Where the E10 finally stops, A is a preserved fishing village of rorbuer, drying racks, and small museums documenting Lofoten's cod-fishing heritage. Just past Moskenes and its mainland ferry, it feels like the literal end of the road, quiet, historic, and steeped in the working traditions of the sea.
pros: Near the Moskenes ferry to the mainland
cons: Long drive from larger towns and airports
